subtitulo: Italian is spelled the way it sounds and sounds the way it is spelled — the four moves that make your first words land
cena: The barista has already turned toward the machine and is waiting for one word she can act on.
frasePiso: Say every vowel, double every double, and land the stress where the word puts it. That is enough to be understood on day one.

steps.pt: Good news: Italian is written the way it sounds. Four moves, and words you half-know start landing.
Five clean vowels. No sliding, no swallowing — each one holds its shape.
First move: every vowel gets said. English eats word endings; Italian does not. Pane is PA-ne, both halves.
A coffee, please. Four syllables in per favore — none of them dropped.

steps.promptPt: At the counter, order one coffee. Say every syllable. Speak now.
steps.pt: A coffee, please.
Second: the double consonant is real. Nono is ninth, nonno is grandfather. Hold the double a beat longer.
I'd like a beer. Two doubles: vorrei and birra. Lean on both.

steps.promptPt: Order a beer, holding both double letters. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'd like a beer.
Third: c and g go soft before e and i — ciao, gelato. Before a, o and u they stay hard.
A chocolate gelato. Soft g, soft c — and a double k sound in the middle.

steps.promptPt: Order a chocolate gelato. Soft g, soft c. Speak now.
steps.pt: A chocolate gelato.
Fourth: stress lands on the second-to-last syllable. When it does not, the written accent tells you.
Where is the station? Note the ts sound in -zione, and the stress on O.

steps.promptPt: Ask where the station is. The accent on è tells you where to land. Speak now.
steps.pt: Where is the station?
Straight ahead, then right.

steps.promptPt: Thank them. Two words, both vowels landed. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much.

steps.promptPt: Greet the barista before you order anything. Speak now.
steps.pt: Good morning!

steps.promptPt: Ask for water. Hold the double c in acqua’s cousin — say every vowel. Speak now.
steps.pt: A glass of water, please.

steps.promptPt: You lost the answer. Ask them to repeat more slowly. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you repeat that, please?

steps.es: Un caffè, per favore. Vorrei una birra. Dov'è la stazione? Grazie mille.
steps.pinyin: oon kaf-FEH per fa-VO-re. vor-RAY oo-na BEER-ra. do-VEH la sta-tsee-O-ne. GRA-tsee-eh MEEL-le
steps.pt: Shadow all four moves in one run.
steps.tts: Un caffè, per favore. Vorrei una birra. Dov'è la stazione? Grazie mille.

steps.pt: B01 done. Every vowel said, doubles held, c and g soft before e and i, stress where the accent puts it.

aprofundar.titulo: The sound model this course uses

secoes.corpo: Unlike English or French, Italian is close to phonetic: once you know the letters, you can pronounce a word you have never seen. That is why this part is four rules and not a chapter — the payoff per rule is unusually high.

exemplos.pt: sta-tsee-O-ne — zi is a ts sound
NYOK-kee — gn is like the ny in canyon

secoes.corpo: It is not decoration. Nono (ninth) and nonno (grandfather), pena (sorrow) and penna (pen), casa (house) and cassa (till). Holding the double is the difference between two real words.

The default is the second-to-last syllable. When a word breaks the default, Italian writes the accent for you: caffè, città, perché, così. The written accent is a gift — it is the language telling you where to push.

A rolled r you cannot roll is not a travel emergency. Clear vowels, held doubles and correct stress buy far more intelligibility than performing an accent. The target is understood the first time, not mistaken for a local.

permissao: You are allowed to sound foreign. Nobody at that counter is grading your r. Five clean vowels and the stress in the right place is the whole ask on day one — the rest tidies itself up over the trip.
espelho: English swallows unstressed vowels without anyone noticing — 'chocolate' loses a syllable, 'comfortable' loses two. Italian keeps every one, so the habit that is invisible at home is the single thing that makes a word you both own stop being recognisable.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You say a word you are sure about — pasta, gelato, cappuccino — and the person pauses before answering.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: My accent is so bad that even the easy words fail.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Those words arrived in English with the vowels flattened and the doubles removed. Saying them the English way makes them land as words the listener does not have, rather than as a mispronunciation of words they do.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say it again slightly slower, giving every vowel its full value and holding the double: cap-puc-CI-no.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The dozens of Italian words you already know stop being the ones that fail first.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not at a hotel desk or an airport counter used to international guests, where staff decode accented Italian all day and will get you the first time regardless.
